question: Shanti has three daughters. Their average age of them is 15 years. If she adopted an 11-year-old girl, then new average will be
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Deviation of the newly adopted girl's age from the current average = 11 − 15 = −4 years.

This deficit of 4 years will be shared equally among all 4 girls (3 current + 1 new).

Change in average = −4 ÷ 4 = −1 year.

New average = 15 − 1 = 14 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of current daughters = 3

Average age of the 3 daughters = 15 years

Age of the adopted girl = 11 years

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Total Number of Observations

 Current Daughters & Adopted Girl:
 
 
 15
 
 
 15
 
 
 15
 
 +

 
 11
 
 Sum = 56

 New Average (Equally Distributed):
 
 
 14
 
 
 14
 
 
 14

 
 14
 
 Avg = 14

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 3 daughters = 3 × 15 = 45 years

⇒ Total age of all girls after adoption = 45 + 11 = 56 years

⇒ Total number of girls after adoption = 3 + 1 = 4

⇒ New average age = 56 ÷ 4 = 14 years

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with an average of A₁, and group 2 has n₂ items with an average of A₂, then the Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Average Replacement

If an existing person is replaced by a new person and the overall average increases by x, the new person's value = Old person's value + (Total persons × x).

Effect of Arithmetic Operations

If each given observation in a set is systematically increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant value 'k', then the average of the set will also undergo the same exact operation by 'k'.
